newsitem.title: CUBA: German held over tunnel blast deported from Cuba.
newsitem.headline: German held over tunnel blast deported from Cuba.

text.p: A German tourist held for five days by Cuban police after he detonated a firework rocket in a traffic tunnel under Havana Bay was being released and would leave Cuba on Thursday, the Cuban Foreign Ministry said.

"A German citizen was arrested when he detonated an artefact in the Havana tunnel...he is leaving the country today," ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol told reporters at the Foreign Ministry's weekly news briefing.

She did not name the man but diplomatic sources identified him as Michael Andreas Reeb, who was detained last Saturday after setting off what Ferriol described as "a kind of rocket" in the traffic tunnel that runs under Havana Bay. No damage or injuries were reported.
She made clear that the device he used was a firework of the kind employed to celebrate events and festivities in some countries.
Ferriol said the Cuban and German authorities had reached a "joint decision" that Reeb would fly out of Cuba on Thursday. "You can't call it an expulsion," she said.
The ministry spokeswoman said it was not the first time that Reeb had let off such devices on the island but did not elaborate further.
She did not link this incident to two small bombs that exploded in two central Havana hotels last July 12, slightly injuring three people.

Cuba's Interior Ministry said the July 12 explosions were caused by "explosive artefacts" and said it had evidence to show that the people responsible for placing them and the material used came from the United States.
The U.S. government has asked Cuba to produce the evidence to back this accusation.
